name: Morda

attributes.attribute: a minor Welsh hero who was an old man tending the fire below Ceridwen's cauldron
tasted the magical brew and took the wisdom while a blind servant did not see

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Morda was a minor hero in Welsh mythology. He was an old man whose duty was to tend the fire beneath the great cauldron of the goddess Ceridwen. She kept the cauldron to brew wisdom and knowledge. A blind servant beside the cauldron failed to see Gwion taste the magical brew. Gwion took the wisdom from the cauldron unseen, and the servant noticed nothing. Ceridwen grew furious at the theft. She struck Morda so hard that one of his eyes fell out.
objective: Document the Welsh hero Morda and Ceridwen's cauldron.
key_results: Record Morda as a minor Welsh hero tending Ceridwen's fire.
Record Gwion taking the wisdom from the cauldron unseen.
Record Ceridwen's blow that knocked out one of Morda's eyes.
